A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECTS taxonomy and benchmark study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. v1 Appendices A–B correspond to v3 Appendices B–C, with a new hyperparameters appendix in v3.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original benchmark results and analyses of calibration, classifier choice, normalization and cost settings.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original benchmark results and supplementary analyses. Figure 3 additionally reports classification accuracy over time for SmoothSubspace.

M1.justification: The trigger procedures, Proba Threshold baseline and Teaser variants are retained. Renaming cost-aware methods as cost-informed and providing additional settings do not establish an algorithmic change. No procedural change is documented to explain the revised Calimera result.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 77-dataset UCR benchmark and 35-dataset non-z-normalized collection, with matching exclusions and cost scenarios. SmoothSubspace was already included in v1; its new illustration adds analysis within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator set, including both Teaser variants and the ASAP, ALAP and Proba Threshold baselines. Benefitter and Ringel et al.'s approach are added to the literature discussion, without being added to the benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The new SmoothSubspace diagnostic uses spline-transformed inputs, a linear ridge model and Platt scaling to report class-specific and overall accuracy across timestamps. The main benchmark retains its splits, MiniROCKET classifier, cost settings and alpha grid; the new hyperparameter table principally documents existing settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.1.5 and Figure 3 add a dataset-suitability analysis illustrating how predictive information emerges over time. The calibration, classifier-substitution, normalization and cost-component analyses already present in v1 Appendix B are retained in v3 Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report 90% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples, Wilcoxon-Holm comparisons and appendix pairwise p-values and win/tie/loss counts. Expanded captions explain statistics already reported in v1; no new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice is established.

E6.justification: Under the same stated anomaly setting at alpha = 0.5, Calimera's mean AvgCost changes from 6.56 in v1 Figure 6b to 6.02 in v3 Figure 7b, and its rank ordering relative to Stopping Rule changes. Figure 3 also adds SmoothSubspace accuracy trajectories. Most other reported results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.2.1 corrects the boundedness statement to apply to weighted AvgCost_alpha, and the exponential-delay expression now explicitly uses t/T in Figure 6a. The introduction also adds formal sequential-testing background, including the i.i.d. assumption and Wald likelihood ratio. The core ECTS derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a principled taxonomy, shared cost-based evaluation, a non-normalized dataset resource and an open-source library. The principal conclusions about simple baselines, anomaly settings and calibration are not redefined.

C2.justification: v3 explains why meaningful ECTS evaluation requires information gain over time and discusses degenerate cases with consistently perfect or random predictions. Appendix C.5 replaces v1's description of normalization as smoothing with rescaling and removes the unsupported computational-cost remark. Existing applicability limitations and future-work directions largely remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A specifies fixed parameters and search ranges, including Economy k = 1–20, Proba Threshold's 40-point grid and Teaser's nu = 1–5. v3 also discloses softmax use in the existing no-calibration analysis. Code/data access information, hardware and reported runtime remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds sequential-decision references, Ringel et al.'s risk-control approach, Benefitter in Table 1, and additional classifier, software and comparison-method citations. These are limited extensions of the existing review and positioning, rather than a replacement of its taxonomy or research agenda.

P1.justification: Local copyediting, terminology standardization and explanatory paragraph revisions occur throughout. The running author headers are corrected and a hyperparameters appendix is inserted, renumbering the existing appendices. The main section order and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds SmoothSubspace Figure 3 and hyperparameter Table 2, expands the literature table and reformats plot labels and legends. Appendix captions become substantially more informative, especially the former 'Heatmap' caption. Existing benchmark and supplementary displays are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: Concrete hyperparameter disclosures and expanded appendix captions make the benchmark easier to reproduce and interpret, while the dataset-suitability illustration adds useful support. These modest gains outweigh localized editorial problems, including incorrect experiment-diagram references and the unresolved 'pas exact' note in Section 3.2. The Calimera numerical revision remains unexplained, limiting what can be concluded from that change.
